title: Settings
nextRecording: Changes will apply to the next recording.

general.uiLanguageHint: Menus, buttons and text in the app, and the language the summary is written in. It doesn't change the meeting language (that's under Transcription).
general.autostartHint: The app will open on its own when you start your computer.
general.analyticsHint: Which features are used, how long meetings last and which version and system you have, with no identifier. Never titles, text, names, notes or audio. They help us decide what to improve.
general.updatesHint: Looks for new versions of the app and the models, and installs them all at once.
general.checkOnOpenHint: GitHub sees your IP address and which version you have. Nothing else is sent.
general.detectMeetingsHint: When another app (Zoom, Meet, Teams…) starts using the microphone, Murmur offers to record.
general.calendarAlerts: Alert When a Calendar Meeting Starts
general.calendarAlertsHint: About 2 minutes before, with a button to start recording. The recording takes the event's title and guests.
general.calendarNeeded: You need to connect your calendar.
general.indicatorHint: A pill on the right of the screen to go back to Murmur, take a screenshot or stop recording. You can drag it.
general.compact: Compact Mode When Clicking the Indicator
general.compactHint: Murmur becomes narrow, next to the call and always on top, with just the notes.
general.showWhatsNewHint: A summary of what each new version brings, the first time you open Murmur.
general.logHint: A file with what Murmur does inside (recordings, models, errors), to send if something goes wrong. It has nothing of what's said in meetings, no titles and no names, and it doesn't leave your computer unless you send it.
general.feedbackHint: What isn't working, or what you'd like. Quico, who makes Murmur, reads it.

calendar.denied: Denied. Turn on Murmur in System Settings › Privacy & Security › Calendars.
calendar.disconnected: Disconnected: Murmur doesn't read it. macOS still gives it permission; you can remove it in System Settings.
calendar.notConnected: To let you know when a meeting starts and give it the event's title. Read only.
calendar.connected: Connected. Murmur only reads it: it doesn't create or change anything.
calendar.noGuestsHint: By default, only events with guests or a video call link count as meetings.
calendar.emptyHint: Add one in the macOS Calendar app or with an iCal link.
calendar.privacy: Murmur only reads your calendars (title, time, guests and the video call link) to alert you and name the meeting. It never writes anything to them, and the links and the Google access are saved in the system keychain.
calendar.privacyMac: Murmur only reads your calendars (title, time, guests and the video call link) to alert you and name the meeting. It never writes anything to them. The macOS one includes the accounts added in System Settings › Internet Accounts, and the links and the Google access are saved in the keychain.
calendar.googleHint: Sign in with your Google account. It only reads your calendars.
calendar.googleWaiting: Continue in the browser: sign in and allow reading your calendars.
calendar.googleDisconnectMessage: Murmur will stop reading your Google calendars and delete its access from the keychain. The calendars don't change.
calendar.icalHint: Google, Outlook, iCloud or any calendar that gives an .ics link.
calendar.icalLabel: The calendar's link in iCal format
calendar.icalWhere: Where do I find the link?

google.name: Google
steps: Open Google Calendar in your browser and go to Settings (the gear).
On the left, under “Settings for my calendars”, pick the calendar.
Under “Integrate calendar”, copy the “Secret address in iCal format”.

outlook.name: Outlook
steps: Open Outlook in your browser and go to Settings › Calendar › Shared calendars.
Under “Publish a calendar”, pick the calendar and “Can view all details”, then Publish.

icloud.name: iCloud
steps: In the iPhone's Calendar app, tap Calendars and the “i” next to the calendar.
Turn on “Public Calendar” and tap “Share Link” to copy it.
Paste it here: it starts with webcal://.

calendar.icalRemoveMessage: Murmur will stop reading “{{name}}” and delete its link from the keychain. The calendar itself doesn't change.

appearance.themeHint: Each theme has a light and a dark version. The preview shows both.
appearance.appearanceHint: Follow the system or always use light or dark mode.
appearance.primaryPanelHint: The other one shows alongside and can be hidden from the toolbar.

audio.micHint: Your voice and the room's. In a call, it shows up as “You”.
audio.deviceMissing: Not connected: the system one will be used.
audio.inputLevelInUse: The microphone is being used for recording right now.
audio.inputLevelHint: Speak to check that the microphone works.
audio.systemHint: Zoom, Meet, Teams… It's transcribed separately from the microphone and echo is removed, even with speakers. Audio only: Murmur doesn't see your screen.
audio.saveAudioHint: Compressed as Opus, one channel per source (about 11 MB per hour).

permissions.title: Permissions
permissions.micDenied: Denied. Turn on Murmur in System Settings › Privacy & Security › Microphone.
permissions.micUndetermined: You haven't allowed it yet. macOS will ask you.
permissions.systemAudioDenied: Denied. Turn on Murmur in System Settings › Screen & System Audio Recording › System Audio Recording Only.
permissions.systemAudioUndetermined: To hear the other side of calls. macOS will ask you.
permissions.systemAudioGranted: To hear the other side of calls. Audio only: Murmur doesn't see your screen.
permissions.screenHint: Only for the screenshots you take from the indicator. Murmur never records your screen.

languages.caHint: When it's over, the BSC's Catalan Whisper listens to the meeting again and rewrites the text (about 11 minutes per hour of meeting), and Softcatalà's model adds punctuation and capitals. If Spanish is spoken, choose “Catalan + Spanish”: Whisper would turn it into Catalan.
languages.esHint: When it's over, Whisper listens to the meeting again and rewrites the text with punctuation and capitals (about 6 minutes per hour of meeting).
languages.caEsHint: Understands both languages, even mixed in the same sentence. When it ends, Whisper listens to the meeting again sentence by sentence: the Catalan ones with the Catalan Whisper and the Spanish ones with the general one (about 15 minutes per hour of meeting).
languages.enHint: Parakeet, by NVIDIA, transcribes live. When it's over, Whisper listens to the meeting again and rewrites the text (about 6 minutes per hour of meeting).

transcription.whisperCaPurpose: For meetings in Catalan, including those that mix it with Spanish
transcription.whisperPurpose: For Spanish and English, to tell the language of each sentence in mixed meetings, and to guess the language of audio files
transcription.voiceSaved: Saved on {{date}}. Murmur recognizes you as “You” in every meeting. Only on this computer.
transcription.voiceNone: Read a sentence and Murmur will recognize you as “You”, even when there's more than one of you on the microphone.
transcription.voiceDeleteMessage: Murmur will stop recognizing you automatically. You can record it again whenever you like.
transcription.roomSpeakers: There Are Other People in the Room with Me
transcription.roomSpeakersHint: In a call, everything coming through the microphone is “You”. Turn this on if more than one person is in front of the same computer.
transcription.thresholdHint: Higher separates voices more; lower groups them.
transcription.verifySpeakersHint: Analyzes the whole meeting again to separate voices better. It can take a few minutes (about 7 per hour of meeting), but you can keep working meanwhile.
transcription.finalPassHint: When a meeting finishes, Whisper listens to the audio again and rewrites the text: about 11 minutes per hour in Catalan, about 6 in Spanish or English and about 15 when it mixes Catalan and Spanish, since it goes sentence by sentence. Turn it off to keep the live text.
transcription.punctuateHint: Adds periods, commas and capitals to meetings in Catalan, also after the Catalan Whisper, and to those mixing Catalan and Spanish. In Spanish and English they're already there. Takes a few seconds.
transcription.saveMarkdownHint: When it ends, Murmur writes the meeting as Markdown (.md). While recording, you can change it for that meeting from the top bar.
transcription.markdownFolderDialog: Folder for the meetings' Markdown files
transcription.glossaryHint: Names, brands and acronyms the transcription gets wrong. Murmur will write them as you put them here, live and when it finishes. Capitals follow too: if you add an everyday word, like “Mark”, it will change everywhere.
transcription.glossaryEmpty: No words yet. You can also add them when you correct a sentence in the transcript.
transcription.markdownContentHint: “Everything” saves two files: the summary with the notes, and the transcript. If a meeting has no summary, everything goes in one.
transcription.askAfterHint: A card above the meeting says what it'll do, and you can change it. If you touch nothing, it starts by itself after 10 seconds.
transcription.summarizeHint: Title, summary, decisions and tasks, with the model chosen in Intelligence.

intelligence.summarize: Generate the Summary When Recording Ends
intelligence.summarizeHint: A language model reads the transcript and writes the title, summary, decisions, tasks and sections. You can keep working meanwhile.
intelligence.privacy: Everything happens on this computer: the transcript never leaves it. Models are only downloaded if you turn the feature on, and you can delete them whenever you want.
intelligence.coverLanguageHint: In the meeting's language, “Catalan + Spanish” is written in Catalan. Meetings recorded before this version use the interface language.
intelligence.engineCloud: In the cloud, with your key
intelligence.engineLocalHint: Gemma, on the computer. The transcript stays here, but it takes about 2–3 minutes for a 20-minute meeting.
intelligence.engineCloudHint: Faster and better, but the transcript is sent to {{provider}}. You need your own API key, billed separately by usage.
intelligence.privacyCloud: Each time a summary is generated, the transcript's text and the notes are sent to {{provider}}. The audio never leaves this computer, and the key is saved in the macOS keychain.
intelligence.privacyRouter: Each time a summary is generated, the transcript's text and the notes are sent to OpenRouter, which passes them on to the company behind the model you chose. The audio never leaves this computer, and the key is saved in the keychain.

model.deleteMessage: {{name}} ({{size}}) will be deleted. You can download it again whenever you want.
model.notDownloadable: Can't be downloaded from the app yet · {{size}}

prompts.title: Summary Prompts
prompts.footnote: Answers always follow the same format (JSON), so you can change the text without breaking the summary. Changes apply to the next summaries.
prompts.needMeeting: Open a finished meeting to try the prompt on it.
prompts.resultTime: Answer in {{seconds}} s · {{tokens}} tokens · {{total}} s total including reading

keyHints.anthropic: A Claude or ChatGPT subscription won't do: you need an API key, billed separately by usage.
keyHints.openai: A Claude or ChatGPT subscription won't do: you need an API key, billed separately by usage.
keyHints.gemini: A Gemini subscription won't do: you need an API key. There's a free tier with limits, and beyond that it's billed by usage.
keyHints.openrouter: OpenRouter runs on prepaid credit: you add money and each summary uses a little. One key gives you models from many companies.

cloud.keySaved: Key saved in the keychain, ending in …{{hint}}
cloud.disconnectMessage: The {{company}} key will be removed from the keychain. Your existing summaries don't change.
cloud.modelHint: Larger ones write better and cost more per summary.

share.intro: Meetings are shared through a Worker on your Cloudflare account, which is free. Murmur publishes it and encrypts them before sending: not even Cloudflare can read them.
share.keySaved: Key saved in the keychain, ends in …{{hint}}
share.disconnectMessage: Links you've already shared will keep working, but you won't be able to create or withdraw any until you connect it again.
share.privacy: Only what you choose when sharing is sent, encrypted on this Mac. The audio only if you tick it.
share.publishedHint: On your Cloudflare account. Murmur keeps it up to date.
share.notReadyYet: It's published. The first time, the address can take a few minutes to start working.
share.step1Hint: Cloudflare opens with the form filled in. If you don't have an account, it will ask you to create one, for free. At the end, press “Create Token” and copy it.
share.tokenHint: It's only allowed to use Workers and KV. Murmur keeps it in the keychain to keep the Worker up to date.
share.manual: I already have a Worker published with setup.sh

claude.intro: With the connector, Claude can read and search your meetings and transcribe audio on this Mac with Murmur. Transcription happens here, and Claude only gets the text it asks for.
claude.desktopHint: Murmur is added to Claude Desktop's settings. Then reopen it.
claude.desktopOnHint: Connected. If Claude Desktop was open, reopen it so it finds Murmur.
claude.desktopMissing: Claude Desktop isn't on this Mac. You can also use it with Claude Code.
claude.desktopAdded: Murmur was added to Claude Desktop. Reopen it so it finds Murmur.
claude.desktopRemoved: Murmur is no longer in Claude Desktop.
claude.manualHint: In Claude Desktop, go to Settings › Developer › Edit Config and add this to the file:
claude.codeHint: Paste this command in Terminal. Murmur will be available in all your projects:
claude.codeCheck: To check, type /mcp in Claude Code: “murmur” should be listed.
claude.ask2: “What did we decide with Acme last week?”
claude.ask3: “Which tasks are still open from this month's meetings?”
claude.ask4: “Search my meetings for when we talked about the budget.”
claude.tools: Claude does it with five Murmur tools: list, search and read meetings, transcribe a file and check on it. The first time, it asks your permission for each one. A long transcription takes a few minutes, and Claude checks how it's going.
claude.privacy: Murmur sends nothing on its own: Claude only gets the text it asks the tools for, and handles it under your terms with Anthropic. Audio never leaves the Mac.

mobile.intro: Connect Murmur for phone to this computer: meetings you record on it arrive here on their own for the final pass and the summary, and the result goes back to the phone.
mobile.history: This computer's meetings on the phone
mobile.historyHint: Only the text, speakers, notes and summary, without the audio. They arrive the next time the phone syncs. Needs Murmur for mobile 1.1 or later.
mobile.unpairMessage: Meetings already synced stay on both. To connect it again you'll need a new code.
mobile.scanTitle: Scan this code with your phone
mobile.scanHint: Open Murmur on your phone, go to Settings › Computer and point the camera here. It will connect to “{{computer}}”.
mobile.paired: “{{name}}” is now connected to this computer.
mobile.privacy: Your phone and this computer talk directly over your network, encrypted, through no server. Your voiceprint never leaves the device.
mobile.windowsNetwork: If Windows asks whether Murmur can communicate on the network, allow it on private networks. If the phone can't find the computer, check that your Wi-Fi network is set to private (Settings › Network & internet).

export.intro: Where meetings go besides Murmur: Markdown files in a folder, your Obsidian vault and Notion. Each can take every meeting on its own when it ends.
export.folderHint: Inside the vault. Screenshots go to “attachments”, next to it.
export.obsidianAuto: Save Each Meeting When It Ends
export.obsidianAutoHint: Once the final pass and the summary are done. You can also do it from Export.
export.peopleHint: Writes names as [[Marta]]: Obsidian makes a page per person with all their meetings.
export.privacy: Markdown and Obsidian are saved on this computer: nothing goes to the internet.
export.notionConnectHint: Notion opens in your browser: sign in and allow. No key to create.
export.notionWaiting: Waiting for you to allow it in Notion, in your browser…
export.notionConnectedHint: The connection is kept in the keychain and renews itself.
export.notionDisconnectMessage: Meetings you already saved stay in Notion. To save more, you'll need to connect it again.
export.notionAuto: Save Each Meeting When It Ends
export.notionPrivacy: Only the meeting's text (summary, notes and transcript) goes to Notion, straight to your workspace, when you export it or when it ends if that's on. Never the audio or the screenshots.

modelPicker.noneHint: Try the company's name, like “google” or “mistral”.
